messages:
Maya: Quick sync — onboarding progress persistence for first-run checklist. Do we auto-save every step (so users can leave & come back) or keep an explicit 'Save & Continue' CTA? Thinking about predictability and privacy.
Liam: leaning auto-save. Users expect modern apps to preserve state. reduces friction for demos. :raised_hands:
Sophia: +1 auto-save for the flow, but can we show a subtle toast: "Progress saved"? Avoid full-screen modals when they leave.
Omar: technically easy if we scope to browser storage (localStorage) or cookies, but for signed-in users we could persist server-side too. server persistence adds product complexity (versioning the checklist).
Maya: good point. For private deployments (enterprise) server persistence may be required for seat handoffs. Can we default to client-side and provide opt-in server sync?
Nora: accessibility note — if we auto-save, ensure screen reader gets an announcement when progress is saved. Use aria-live="polite" for the toast and avoid focus traps.
Sophia: agree. Also add a keyboard shortcut to manually save/continue for power users (e.g., Ctrl+Enter) and surface it in the toast.
Omar: rough engineering approach: client-side key name `redwood_onboard_v2`. If user is authenticated and opts into sync we POST to /api/onboarding/progress. Example payload snippet: ```{"step":3,"completed":true,"timestamp":1710000000}```. We should version the payload.
Liam: UX question — do we show a progress pill in the console header reflecting saved state? Might help users see where they left off across devices (if server-sync).
Maya: prefer showing a small status dot + percent in the quickstart rail. But default to hidden unless server-sync enabled. Keep header uncluttered.
Nora: also ensure color contrast for the progress pill meets WCAG. If we use green for saved, double-check against dark/light themes.
Sophia: copy microcopy: toast text = "Progress saved — you can continue anytime." CTA on toast: "Continue setup" (primary) and "Turn off sync" (link-style). If not authed, show "Sign in to sync progress across devices."
Omar: implementation concern: avoid race conditions when user has multiple tabs. Client can use `storage` events to sync tab state; server-side we need optimistic concurrency via last-write-wins and store a `client_id` and `modified_at`.
Liam: small behavior nit — if user completes checklist and then opts out of sync, should we keep completed state locally? I think yes, but server should delete remote copy if they explicitly disable sync.
Maya: policy agreed: default = client-only auto-save. If user signs in, prompt once: "Sync onboarding progress to your account?" (Yes/No). If Yes -> enable server sync. If No -> keep client-only.
Nora: add accessibility acceptance criteria to the ticket: toast aria-live, keyboard shortcut, focus does not jump, progress indicator labeled for screen readers ("Onboarding progress: 40% complete").
Sophia: I'll draft the mock with a micro-interaction for the toast and a small progress pill variant. Will also include the copy variants for the sign-in prompt.
Maya: awesome — Omar, can you estimate effort for client-only + opt-in server-sync?
Omar: client-only: 1.5 dev days (incl. storage events + tests). Server-sync opt-in + api + migration: 3.5 dev days + 1 day backend review. Total ~6 dev days.
Maya: thanks. I'll create a ticket with the ACs (including Nora's a11y items) and the copy variants. Sophia, drop your mock in the thread when ready.
Sophia: will do. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Maya: flagged. If the team agrees on default flow, we'll aim to land client-only auto-save before that window.
Liam: quick +1 from me.
Omar: same.
Nora: +1 on a11y checks.
Sophia: +1 — will include keyboard flow in the mock.
